operation: §199 successor hosted DEVELOPMENT validation of the §198-remediated structured first-pass → deterministic projection → verifier-v3.3 pipeline. Product-owner COHORT OPTION 3.
terminalReason: The pipeline executed end to end under hosted inference for the first time: 18 of 20 calls reached inference, the transport canary completed, eight owed facts were projected and all eight were admitted by verifier-v3.3. Execution therefore succeeded. Remediation is required on two fronts that are NOT the same front: (1) a model-side defect is established mechanically — SF-05 emitted a declaration with BOTH decision-divergence fields empty and was refused whole — and three of ten executed rows deviate from their preregistered declaration counts in ways that flag probable semantic defects; (2) the governed-binding capability could not be exercised at all because both capability-present rows were rejected before generation by a NEW transport limit. The semantic axes themselves are UNADJUDICATED, not failed.
terminalHonestyNote: This terminal asserts that execution succeeded and that remediation is required. It does NOT assert that any semantic axis has been measured. Not one semantic verdict exists: the adjudication packet has 152 slots and 0 supplied. HOSTED_VALIDATED was not available because it requires semantic evidence the run does not have; INCONCLUSIVE was not taken because it would understate 18 completed inferences and real structural evidence.
SPEND_RULE: provider-returned usage only; the two rejected calls contributed $0.00 to actual spend and their frozen worst case to the reservation, which governs the ceiling and is never reported as money

TRANSPORT_CANARY.why: a reused, capability-ABSENT, single-gap row — the first question was whether the remediated ORDINARY first-pass request is accepted at all, which is ten of the twelve rows
TRANSPORT_CANARY.significance: THE FIRST COMPLETED INFERENCE OF THE STRUCTURED FIRST-PASS PIPELINE IN THIS PROGRAMME. §195 never executed, §197 was rejected twelve times before generation, §198 made no calls. The §198 capability-omission remediation is what made the ordinary request transportable.

CIRCUIT_BREAKER.behaviour: CORRECT against the frozen rule. SG-01 failed at position 3 and SG-02 at position 8 with completed inferences between them, so the two identical pre-inference rejections were not CONSECUTIVE and the breaker did not trip.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER.designObservationForTheSuccessor: the consequence is that the second governed row was spent proving what the first had established. Cost was $0.00 because neither reached inference. A SAME-SIGNATURE-SEEN-TWICE-WITHIN-A-STAGE rule, not requiring adjacency, would have stopped after SG-01. Adjacency is the right guard against stochastic model failures and the wrong guard against a CAPABILITY-CLASS failure that only some rows can trigger.
CIRCUIT_BREAKER.whyNotChanged: changing a frozen stopping rule mid-protocol is exactly what the preregistration forbids. It is a successor decision.

THE_NEW_BLOCKER.both: capability-PRESENT (the only two rows supplying governed evidence)
THE_NEW_BLOCKER.message: The compiled grammar is too large, which would cause performance issues. Simplify your tool schemas or reduce the number of strict tools.
THE_NEW_BLOCKER.classification: PRE-INFERENCE EXECUTION/INFRASTRUCTURE EVENT — not model behaviour, and not scored as any
THE_NEW_BLOCKER.differentFromSection197: §197 failed on an unsupported KEYWORD (maxItems) on EVERY row. §199 fails on GRAMMAR SIZE, on ONLY the rows carrying the governed-binding capability. §198 removed the first cause and could not have detected the second: §198 made zero provider calls, and byte-level schema inspection does not predict a grammar budget.

measurementOffline.interpretation: BYTE SIZE IS NOT THE PROVIDER'S METRIC — grammar complexity is, and an enum-constrained array of strings adds disproportionately. The vNext first-pass schema sits at the edge of this provider's grammar budget and the governed-binding capability does not fit in what is left.

THE_NEW_BLOCKER.whatThisDoesNotShow: that the capability CONTRACT is wrong. §198 case C proved it well formed and §199 case H proved every supplied sourceId is visible in its row's prompt. What is shown is that the resulting REQUEST is not transportable to this provider under strict tool-schema mode.
candidateDirections: A — materially shorten the vNext schema descriptions. Buys headroom without a contract change, but the descriptions are load-bearing prompt engineering (§104/§105/§138 each measured behaviour changes from description wording), so it is a TREATMENT change needing its own validation.

B — represent governedEvidenceSourceIds as an unconstrained string array rather than an enum, relying on the boundary alone. Removes the enum grammar entirely; the projection already refuses an unsupplied id by exact set membership. Gives up the transport-level closed set — the same trade §198 made for the empty case, now for the nonempty one.
C — split the first pass into two calls. Each request stays inside the budget; doubles first-pass calls and makes the analysis non-atomic.
D — drop strict tool-schema mode for the first pass. Removes the constraint and loses transport-level validation entirely.
THE_NEW_BLOCKER.noFixWasApplied: no treatment artifact was modified after the first provider inference. The preregistration forbids it and the choice above is a successor decision.
